decisions.reason: The assembly and drop-retention requirements apply to the enclosure; they do not necessarily alter the power board's dimensions, orientation, connectors, or mounting-hole specifications.
Requiring the case to retain components does not change the established connector placement, alignment, orientation, or cable-routing rules.
The enclosure's assembly and retention behavior does not affect ESP32 pin coverage or the through-hole breakout configuration.
The source does not change the requirement to place the ESP32 antenna at the PCB edge or establish any new RF-clearance constraint.
The enclosure must secure the existing components, but the source does not change the three-board architecture or the roles and exclusions of its boards.
Simple enclosure assembly and drop retention do not necessarily change the main board's dimensions, prototype adjustability, or routing-space requirement.
The mechanical enclosure decision has no effect on the power board's four-layer stack.
The requirement that all sensor-board content fit remains unchanged by the enclosure's separate assembly and component-retention behavior.
The enclosure design criteria do not alter the JLCPCB order configuration, cart contents, or ordering policies.
The button is already specified as panel-mounted, and the source does not change its connector, electrical behavior, location, or mounting interface.
The enclosure's physical assembly and drop-retention requirements do not change BOM part identification or PCB assembly-readiness rules.
The enclosure decision does not modify the requirement for lead-free manufacturing across the boards.
